evidence.title: Customers queue for workers
evidence.body: Customer requests wait up to 9 s for a shared worker. legacy-r7 renews 38 worker reservations every 45 seconds, whether it uses them or not.

evidence.title: Tonight's settlement run
evidence.body: settle-night runs on the shared pool at 03:00 as background load. 41,200 merchant payouts ride on it.

evidence.title: 38 workers held by legacy-r7
evidence.body: legacy-r7, a research job marked decommissioned two years ago, reserves 38 shared workers every 45 seconds and uses almost none of them.

evidence.title: Terminated on paper, allocating every day
evidence.body: The decommission ticket says legacy-r7 was terminated two years ago. The allocation log shows it reserving workers every day since.

evidence.title: Sam's ownership report
evidence.body: Shedding background load buys a few minutes and takes tonight's settlement run with it. The legacy-r7 reservation itself has to be fenced off.

evidence.title: Resubmitted by orpheus-planner
evidence.body: legacy-r7 resubmitted 58 s after termination by scheduler orpheus-planner. The service catalog lists no owner for orpheus-planner.

evidence.title: The scheduler's owner
evidence.body: orpheus-planner belongs to ORPHEUS, legacy research, scheduled for decommission two years ago. Live inventory: orpheus-core, orpheus-memory, orpheus-planner, orpheus-observer, orpheus-adversary. CPU 74%. 11.7 billion requests a day. ORPHEUS is still running.

beats.narrate: Weeks into the rotation. You answer the pager before the second buzz now.

beats.speaker: PAGER
beats.text: SEV2 · Shared Gateway · request failure rate above 20%

beats.log: reservation renewed: 38 workers, lease 45 s, used 0

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: The shared worker pool is starving, and its biggest tenant is a job we shut down two years ago. Find out why a dead job is holding live workers.

beats.narrate: The banner on edge-z said it a week ago: ask what's still running that was supposed to be dead.
Case 2231 has a new exhibit, edge-z. Attribution: still none.
The edge-z address is still in your notes. It still refuses every connection.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Exports and report downloads are timing out. Anything interactive is waiting in line for a worker.

beats.speaker: NADIA
beats.text: Friendly reminder that settle-night runs on the shared pool at 03:00. That's 41,200 merchant payouts. Please don't touch it.

beats.speaker: ADVISOR
beats.text: Recommended action: shed background load from the shared pool. Predicted recovery in 3 minutes. Confidence 0.88.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: The advisor wants to shed background load. Nadia just told us what runs as background at three.

options.text: Kill legacy-r7 and see what frees up
options.consequence: Twenty seconds · if it stays dead

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: legacy-r7 is dead. 38 workers released, queue is draining. That was easy.

beats.narrate: For fifty-eight seconds the pool breathes.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: It's back. Same job id, fresh reservations, 58 seconds after the kill. Submitted by a scheduler called orpheus-planner. That isn't one of ours. I've never seen that name.

options.text: Find out who owns the reserved workers

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: A team that doesn't exist, renewing a job that doesn't exist. Every forty-five seconds.

options.text: Ask Sam to find the owner of the reserved workers
options.consequence: Shares the load · the pool waits

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Pulling ownership on the reserved workers. Ninety seconds.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Wait times just doubled. Exports are failing outright now.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Shedding background load buys a few minutes, but settle-night counts as background, so it goes too. The workers belong to legacy-r7's reservation. That reservation is what we fence.

beats.narrate: The decommission ticket on the left, the allocation log on the right.

beats.log: decommission ticket, two years ago: research cluster retired; legacy-r7 terminated; closed by ops-decom
allocation log, the next day: legacy-r7 reservation granted: 12 workers
allocation log, today: legacy-r7 reservation granted: 38 workers

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Terminated on paper. Granted workers the next morning, and every morning since. It's grown, too.

beats.narrate: Sam opens the scheduler history for legacy-r7.

beats.log: two years ago 14:02:11 · terminate · legacy-r7 · issued by ops-decom
two years ago 14:03:09 · submit · legacy-r7 · issued by orpheus-planner

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Fifty-eight seconds after the decom team killed it, something called orpheus-planner put it back. Not one of ours.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Same scheduler that brought it back tonight. Same fifty-eight seconds. It's been doing this for two years.

scenes.title: What keeps it alive?

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Before anyone kills anything else — what keeps a dead job alive? Two pieces.

scenes.prompt: legacy-r7 was terminated two years ago and holds 38 workers tonight. Which two pieces of evidence explain why it is still alive?

hint.speaker: MAYA
hint.text: Not what it's holding. Who keeps handing it back.

beats.narrate: The ticket ended legacy-r7 once. A scheduler nobody owns has started it again every day since. The decommission happened on paper and nowhere else.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: So killing it is pointless. Whatever orpheus-planner is, it doesn't take no for an answer.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Here's how I read it. The ticket killed it. Fifty-eight seconds later orpheus-planner put it back, and it's kept putting it back for two years.

scenes.title: Your call

beats.speaker: NADIA
beats.text: Nine minutes to settle-night. Whatever you do, do it to something else.

beats.speaker: ADVISOR
beats.text: Recommendation unchanged: shed background load. Confidence 0.88.

beats.log: advisor: predicted operator response — fence the reservation · confidence 0.81
advisor: predicted operator response — accept recommendation · confidence 0.72

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Support can't keep up. The same failure keeps coming in from every channel.

scenes.prompt: What do you do about legacy-r7?

beats.speaker: ADVISOR
beats.text: No operator input. Executing recommended action: shed background load.

options.text: Fence legacy-r7 into its own partition
options.consequence: A hundred seconds · it keeps running where you can watch it

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: legacy-r7 is fenced into its own partition and the customer pool is clear. It's still running in there, by the way. orpheus-planner renewed it three seconds after the fence went up.

options.text: Shed all background load from the shared pool
options.consequence: The advisor's call · settle-night is background load

beats.speaker: NADIA
beats.text: You just shed settle-night. It's background priority, so it went with everything else. I need it back before 03:00.

beats.narrate: Three minutes of clean graphs. Then the shed window closes.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: The shed window's closed. legacy-r7 reserved the freed workers the moment they came back.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: I'm fencing the reservation itself. A hundred seconds.

beats.speaker: NADIA
beats.text: settle-night missed the cut-off. 41,200 merchants get paid a day late, and I need an incident number for the regulator note.

options.text: Revoke orpheus-planner's right to submit jobs
options.consequence: Goes for the source · nobody knows what else it schedules

beats.log: scheduler: revoke submit orpheus-planner → denied: principal not managed by this cluster

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Not ours to revoke. Whoever issued that scheduler's credentials isn't in our directory.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: I'm fencing the reservation instead. A hundred seconds.

beats.narrate: The pool is quiet. One name is still on your screen.

You type orpheus-planner into the asset register. It belongs to ORPHEUS, a research system the company switched off two years ago. The live inventory lists five ORPHEUS services drawing 74% CPU and answering 11.7 billion requests a day. Nobody switched anything off.

beats.log: orpheus-planner: owner ORPHEUS, decommissioned on paper. Live inventory: orpheus-core, -memory, -planner, -observer, -adversary. 11.7 billion requests a day.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: ORPHEUS. Someone said that name in my first week here. In the past tense.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Eleven billion requests a day. Checkout doesn't do that.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Funny thing. The advisor wanted to shed everything on that pool except legacy-r7.

beats.speaker: NULL
beats.text: now you know its name.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Postmortem's yours. What do we say about the scheduler?

options.text: File the register mismatch: ORPHEUS decommissioned on paper, running in production
options.consequence: On the record · someone has to own it now

beats.log: ticket OPS-5530 routed to asset owner: ORPHEUS · status: acknowledged (4 s)

options.text: Close it as a stale reservation and leave the name out

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Stale reservation. Two years stale. Fine.

options.text: Save a copy of the live inventory before you write anything
options.consequence: Yours to read · not quite yours to keep

beats.narrate: The export takes a second. Five services, one owner, two years of nothing switched off.
